frames.narration: A batch job has 100 records. 10 are permanently malformed and 10 fail a few times, then work. When a record fails, the worker has to decide what happens next.
Strategy 1, swallow and continue: catch every error, save a default, move on. The job finishes on time and nobody is told. 20 wrong records are in the store and look like real ones.
Strategy 2, fail fast: stop at the first error. Record 11 is bad, so the job stops there with 10 correct and 90 not processed. The cause is found at once, but a bad record has cost the whole run.

A transient error is different: a short outage clears if you try again. With 3 retries the flaky records succeed, and with no retries, in a run with 20 of 100 flaky, a blip would stop the job at record 2. Retry only what can go away, with a limit.

Strategy 3, dead-letter and continue: bad records are set aside with their error, the rest go on. 90 records are correct, 10 are parked for a person, 119 attempts were made, and an alert fires at record 11.
The over-applied version retries everything, bad data included. The result is the same 90 correct and 10 parked, but 149 attempts instead of 119: 30 retries of records that could never succeed.

Now each record builds on the one before, like a running balance. Parking record 11 and carrying on means every later record is computed on missing input: 10 correct, 80 wrong. Here the safe move is to stop.

Choose by the shape of the work: fail the unit that failed, retry what is transient, set aside independent items, stop when items depend on each other, and never swallow an error without telling someone.
